RECOMMENDATION: The clinical trials with lubiprostone in pediatric patients should start with a dose- escalation study. Tebentafusp demonstrated broad loss of specificity for the target pHLA complex from 1 nM (1,000× MABEL), where consistent evidence of T cell activation (IFNγ release) and/or redirected killing (GrB release) was observed across the different normal cells tested.  Alloreactivity: Most human TCRs only recognize and bind effectively to self-HLA molecules loaded with peptides. A small proportion (less than 10%) of TCRs have the ability to recognize non-self HLA molecules and can induce allorejection. This phenomenon is termed alloreactivity (Murphy, 2016). Tebentafusp was specifically engineered and selected for high affinity binding to the HLA-A*02:01-gp100 peptide complex. Therefore, binding to a non-HLA- A*02 Class I molecule is unlikely to occur or, if it does, would occur at much reduced affinity than that for the target HLA-A*02 molecule.

Trial DNLI-E-0002 in Subjects With MPS II DNLI-E-0002 is an open-label, multiple-cohort study in pediatric subjects with MPS II. Refer to Section 6.2.1 for further details on the study design. Trial DNLI-E-0002 includes multiple cohorts that vary in starting dose, dose-escalation scheme, and maximum dose (see Section 14.2.1 for more discussion on dosing scheme across cohorts). The lowest starting dosage was 3 mg/kg once weekly (QW), and the highest dosage was 30 mg/kg QW. The dosage of 15 mg/kg QW was the targeted therapeutic dosage in all cohorts. The dosing regimens in Trial DNLI-E-0002 were selected primarily based on results from nonclinical pharmacology and toxicology studies: the human-relevant no-observed-adverse-effect level (NOAEL) from toxicology studies was established at 150 mg/kg weekly in both the adult mouse and the monkey as well as 40 mg/kg for the juvenile monkey, which supported the selected clinical doses from a safety perspective. From a PD or efficacy perspective, the starting

toxicology studies was established at 150 mg/kg weekly in both the adult mouse and the monkey as well as 40 mg/kg for the juvenile monkey, which supported the selected clinical doses from a safety perspective. From a PD or efficacy perspective, the starting dose of 3 mg/kg was selected based on data in the MPS II (Ids KO;TfRmu/hu KI) mouse model, which showed that four weekly 3 mg/kg doses of tividenofusp alfa resulted in similar PD effect on liver GAG levels as four weekly 1 mg/kg doses of idursulfase. In addition, 3 mg/kg doses of tividenofusp alfa resulted in reductions in CSF and brain GAGs as well as reductions in CSF and serum NfL levels. The MPS II mouse model showed that four weekly doses of 10 mg/kg tividenofusp alfa resulted in a near-normalization of GAGs and NfL. Clinical Studies Supporting the Efficacy and Safety of Olipudase in Pediatric Patients: The clinical drug development program for Olipudase included a total of 10 studies in patients with ASMD.
